name: json-codec-write
algorithm: Decode a 1 MB JSON document (tools/bench gen kind json, seed 2), an array of records, into each language's structs once, then write the structs back as compact JSON into an in-memory buffer reps times through the std's typed encoder (README.md).

skip.c: no std JSON: C has no standard JSON encoder; no library stands in
skip.rust: no std JSON: Rust std has none (serde_json is a crate); no crate stands in
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the writer has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own algorithm; the checksum (reps times the count of the structural bytes { } [ ] : , and " in the last output) checks that every encoder wrote the same records, keys and strings, whatever digits its float formatting chooses
notes: Idiomatic standard library (plan/06-m6.md 4.1): Mk the FormatJson that gen json.Codec emits per record, between "[", "," and "]" written by the program, into a Text through its Writer, cleared per rep; Go encoding/json Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) of []R0 into a bytes.Buffer reset per rep; Zig std.json.Stringify.valueAlloc of []R0 into an ArenaAllocator reset per rep. The decode runs once and is outside what the reps measure, but inside the program's time (../codec times it). Bytes per second = output length x reps / median.
